terra.problem: The explanation introduces Moses as Israel's leader without a reference for that fact outside the passage.
Paul says his readers can read and understand what he writes; he does not say his letters contain no codes or riddles.
Saying Paul is not trying to impress anyone assigns him a motive the text does not give.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the route, with little of Papa Dorin's personality.
The cookie-box comparison makes God's handling of His promises part of the joke, rather than keeping the humor on the human side.
Paul says all God's promises are Yes in Christ; he does not say God gives out all or most of an individual promise.
Calling it a good list is generic and adds little warmth or insight to the explanation.
A pledge here is a guarantee of what is to come; calling it a promise held in advance blurs the distinction between the Spirit and what the Spirit guarantees.
The definition of a pledge as a promise held in advance blurs the distinction between the Spirit and what the Spirit guarantees.
Paul does not say he cannot be cheered from far away. The distance is added to his point.
The text gives Paul's stated purpose, but does not say whether he was trying to scold or establish that tears and anguish rule that out.
Saying the church felt grief 'too' adds that Paul was grieved, although he says the person has not grieved him but all of them, to some degree.
Saying Paul has plenty to be sore about attributes a feeling to him without marking it as a guess.
The text says Paul wrote to see whether they would stand the test; it does not say the letter had a test in it.
Forgiving in Christ's presence does not establish that the forgiveness was not done in secret.
Paul speaks of Satan not outwitting them, not of staying out of Satan's way.
